about: Documented GTK limits (docs/developer/kit/lumaui-deviations.md) that lumaui-conform reports as 'accepted' instead of failing. Each entry is narrow: optional states, group, subject and prop regexes, and max_delta (the largest difference it forgives). Add one only with a matching row in lumaui-deviations.md.

deviations.doc: lumaui-deviations.md: Toast, action bar, content-lit card, scrim / Action center
deviations.reason: GTK has no backdrop-filter; the kit paints a denser token surface, so the sampled surface colour differs a little.
deviations.subject: corner pill|toast|bar

deviations.doc: lumaui-deviations.md: Event card, content-lit header wash / Person avatar
deviations.reason: No runtime oklch(): avatars and the hero wash use the five category hues, not the person's exact hue.
deviations.subject: ^(box|generic) "[A-Z]{1,2}"$|hero light

deviations.reason: In edit mode the name field stays 30/700 (hero role) instead of v70's 26 px input.
deviations.subject: Priya Raman

deviations.doc: lumaui-deviations.md: Count badge, pill, stacked button
deviations.reason: GTK has no corner-shape: round; plain radii stand in.
deviations.subject: ^(button|box|card) "(Message|Call|Video|Email|On Luma)"$

deviations.subject: Delete contact|trash-2

deviations.reason: GTK allocates whole pixels; v70's 1.45 line boxes and rows are fractional (49.525, 16.675), so rows drift by up to half a pixel each. The tokens round so a card's or list's first and last rows stay close; what is left is at most 3 px.

v70's LCD asks for var(--mono, ui-monospace); outside Terminal --mono is unset (the LCD, hex colour codes), so Chromium draws the Mac's ui-monospace. Luma's system monospace is IBM Plex Mono (v70 line 745, TY1 mono), which the kit uses.
deviations.subject: ^text "#?[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+"$

deviations.doc: lumaui-deviations.md: Media transport LCD (the same decision: Luma's system monospace)
deviations.reason: v70 asks for ui-monospace, the Mac's system monospace; Chromium resolves it to a platform face. Luma's system monospace is IBM Plex Mono (v70 line 745, TY1 mono), which the kit's mono role draws. Only that pair is accepted: a mono spec face against IBM Plex Mono.

The same texts as system-mono-face: IBM Plex Mono's advance differs from the face Chromium draws for ui-monospace, so a mono value's width, and what follows it on its line, differ by that much. Settings' values only.
deviations.subject: ^text "(lantern-orbit-42|Luma Shell 1\.0 on Wayland|Intel Core Ultra 7 155U × 14|N3XET47W \(1\.22\)|Intel Arc \(MTL\)|Linux 6\.16\.8-luma1|Samsung PM9C1a 512 GB|1\.0 nightly 20260923|[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}|([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}:){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})"$

deviations.reason: A character Figtree lacks (U+23CE ⏎) falls back on both sides; the spec reports the CSS family, GTK the face that drew it.
deviations.subject: ^text "[\u2190-\u23ff\u2700-\u27bf]"$

deviations.reason: Figtree has no non-breaking hyphen (U+2011, v70's "Wi‑Fi"); Pango draws it from the next face in the stack and Chromium from its own fallback, whose advances differ by a few px. The rest of the string is Figtree on both sides.
deviations.subject: ^text ".*‑.*"$

deviations.reason: The device hints Figtree (Nick's setting, the real one): GTK rounds each glyph's advance to whole pixels where Chromium keeps fractions, so a run comes out up to about 3% wider. Text-run width only, Figtree runs only; never boxes, positions of other parts, size or weight.
deviations.subject: ^text

deviations.reason: The same hinted advances: an end-aligned Figtree run keeps its right edge, so its start moves by exactly its own width difference (up to 3%) and nowhere else. Only that shift of that text; never other parts.
deviations.subject: ^text

deviations.reason: PENDING google-figtree-fonts 1.luma.4 (U+2010/U+2011 mapped to Figtree's hyphen). Until it ships, a line holding U+2011 draws its fallback face's taller line box, 1 px, and what follows on Settings' Wi‑Fi pages sits up to 2.5 px lower. Remove when the font is on the ThinkPad.
v70 leaves some inputs on Chromium's placeholder grey #757575, 3.8:1 on the dark well; the coordinator ruled an AA dark value, so @luma_placeholder_ink is #85878b in dark. Only that pair.
